title.reading: つきのいでたらむよは　じゅうごやずり
title.zh: 月出之夜 · 十五夜摺
title.en: On Nights When the Moon Comes Out — A Fifteenth-Night Impression

logline_zh: 十五夜，祖母以初升的明月为灯，把《竹取物语》化作纸门上的影绘；当月亮走进圆窗，她自己的影子离开身体，攀着窗格升入月中，只回头望了一眼。六十个秋天之后，当年的孩子白发苍苍，披着祖母留下的羽织独坐同一条檐廊，在一轮丝毫未老的月亮下把那一夜看完——正如辉夜姬所托：“有月亮出来的夜晚，请望向我。”
logline_en: On the fifteenth night a grandmother turns the Tale of the Bamboo Cutter into shadows on the shoji, with the rising moon as her lantern; when the moon reaches the round window, her own shadow leaves her body, climbs the lattice into it, and looks back once. Sixty autumns later the child, now old, sits alone on the same veranda in her grandmother's haori and finishes the night under a moon that has not aged — doing what Kaguya asked: on nights when the moon comes out, look toward me.
time_convention: Segment 'start'/'end' and every 't_abs' are absolute film seconds. In beats and text_cues, 't' is LOCAL seconds from the segment's start (this is what js/script.js and TSUKI.TEXT consume). Inside layer/moon prose, times are written as local seconds followed by absolute film time in brackets, e.g. '6.5s [124.5]'. In 'audio', 'summary', 'negative_space' and 'transition_out', all times are absolute film seconds. All ambient motion (susuki sway and gusts, kasumi drift, the 7 s kira sweep, glow breathing, insect beds) reads t_abs, never segment-local t, so the seamless hand-offs (序→一, 三→四) continue without a restart.
device: The whole film is ONE woodblock print pulled on the Fifteenth Night, and its printing is the story. (1) 序 teaches the grammar: blank washi, a baren spiral reveals the sumi key block, each colour block lands a few px out of register and settles with a wooden kentō CLICK, and one round patch stays dry — the moon, which is never printed. (2) The grandmother's night (t 14–160) is the 初摺, the first impression: every block, crisp bokashi, fresh pigment. At the moon's culmination (140.0, exactly centred in the round window) the night hinges. (3) On the sōzu's KON at 160.0 the same master shot is pulled again from the worn blocks sixty years later — the 後摺: warm blocks gone, sky flat, key lines broken, registration drifted, paper yellowed and foxed. Only the moon is identical, because an absence cannot wear out. The second half of the moon's arc (culmination → set) belongs to this later night; the join is invisible because the moon does not change. (4) Renderer = plates: every master shot is cached as a key block + colour plates, each drawn per frame with a (dx, dy, alpha) from one table. The same table performs the printing (序), the tears — every colour plate drifting ±6–12 px while the key block holds — and the cold CLICK back into register at 147.8 (五), the jolt into the late impression (六) and the final unprinting in approximately the order pigments fade (結). (5) Transitions between segments are never print-pulls: a seamless hand-off (序→一), sōzu-KON hard cuts (40.0, 160.0), a push-in and match-cut ring→basin (64.0–66.0), the fox window opening inside 三 until it becomes Shot D (88.2–90.0, then a cut), a suyari-gasumi wipe (118–121), a silent cut to A′ (155.0), a cut on falling hands (190.0) and a match-cut incense→Fuji snow gully and smoke on the same axis x 1180 (206.0). (6) Three lenses show the myths without close faces: shoji shadow-play (影絵), water (水鏡), and the fox window (狐の窓), whose diamond clip in 六 re-renders the first-impression scene function at t − 150. (7) Six cached master shots (A wide garden, A′ engawa profile, B shoji wall with round window, C tsukubai, D straight up, E dawn Fuji); たけ and old 小夜 share one figure path. Thesis: お月見 is humanity doing what Kaguya asked — 月の出でたらむ夜は、見おこせたまへ — and those left behind remember on behalf of the one who was made to forget.

palette.use: Washi ground of the 初摺 (first impression). The moon IS this paper: it is never printed, only left bare (a hole through the sky plates: the disc ∩ the shot's sky mask).
The yellowed paper of the 後摺 (sixty years later), applied as a multiply tint everywhere except the moon's disc.
Highlights, snow, the light through puppet slits, kumiko flashes during the climb, dango, kasumi bands, the ribbon of light (天の羽衣), mica (kira) sparkle base.
Moonlit shoji paper; the moon-world; the colour たけ drains to (with 胡粉 and 銀鼠).
The key block, silhouettes, interior darkness, the black 叢雲. As 薄墨 (α 0.06–0.35): smoke, incense, the rabbit's maria (22%).
Clouds, geese, stone, Fuji's smoke thread, far susuki.
Drained colours after the robe; the dawn moon glaze; 後摺 susuki plumes; たけ's hair.
EVERY cast shadow on the shoji (never pure black): the shadow-play, the shadows cast by nothing, the climbing shadow, dawn shadows.
Night sky mid-tones, far hills, 小夜's kasuri kimono, たけ's kimono.
Sky bokashi; the ichimonji band (mixed with 墨 35%); Fuji's massif; Shot D's night.
Water (pond, tsukubai); the ground of the 波兎 haori; the flat pale sky of the 後摺 (α 0.45).
桔梗 flowers in the jug; the pre-dawn band above the 東雲.
Garden greens, susuki stems, moss, reeds, the 萩 branch's leaves.
Susuki plumes, thatch highlights, tatami, 衣かつぎ skins.
聚楽 plaster walls, thatch, earth, the unfaded rectangle; mixed with 墨 (55%) it is the 煤竹 of wood, posts and engawa boards.
The rising moon's glaze and horizon glow; andon-lit shoji; the fire's core; 女郎花; plant-yellow accents.
萩 and 撫子 blossoms (初摺 only; a warm block).
小夜's 紅絞りの兵児帯 (soft red shibori heko-obi — the one colour that survives the drain); the title tanzaku border.
Fire tongues (the only warm colour ever drawn inside the moon); 金木犀 florets; the title seal 縁 (canvas) and the 朱文 seals before 160; the final seal 忘れじ — the first saturated red after 160.
たけ's obijime: a subdued red-brown, right for a woman of 78 (a bright 朱 cord belongs to a young woman). Still warm, so the drain at 155.4 visibly takes it. A mix on plate P2, not a new ink.

ONE ink with two names: the 退紅 of the child's heko-obi faded over sixty years (a strip of it ties the susuki: the single warm spot in the 後摺), and the 東雲 of the final dawn. The dawn is printed in the colour of the faded sash. Every DOM seal after 160 is printed in this faded tone, so 忘れじ is the only fresh 朱.

global_motifs: THE UNBROKEN MOON: one celestial arc for 236 s, never cut, never reprinted, never drawn twice in one frame (the 四 tilt carries one moon from Shot D into Shot A); culminating exactly in the round window at 140.0 and sinking behind Fuji's summit at dawn (hidden 222.6); it falls faster in old age.

THE MOON IS PAPER: never inked — a hole through the sky plates to the washi (the disc ∩ the shot's sky mask, so susuki plumes, mist, lattice and mountain print over it) — except the rabbit's maria, printed from smoke at 106.0 and kept by every later moon. The rabbit earned it.

初摺 / 後摺: the grandmother's night is the first impression (all blocks, bokashi, fresh pigment); sixty years later is a late impression from the worn blocks (warm blocks gone, flat sky, broken lines, drift, foxing). The moon alone is identical in both, because an absence cannot wear out.
MISREGISTRATION = TEARS, CLICK = FORGETTING: the kentō click learned in 序 returns once, at 147.8, when perfect register means the robe has erased her grief.

COLOUR STAYS ON EARTH: the drain turns たけ to 胡粉/銀鼠 while the haori and the child's 紅絞りの兵児帯 keep their colour; in the 後摺 the only warm colour left is a strip of that heko-obi faded to 退紅, tying the susuki (the seals fade to 退紅 with it) — and the dawn is printed in the same ink. The one fresh red after 160 is the final seal 忘れじ.

SHADOW = SOUL, LIGHT = ABSENCE: Kaguya in the shadow-play is a hole cut in paper; the celestials are shadows cast by nothing; たけ's shadow leaves her body; afterwards she casts no shadow while the child does.

ONLY SMOKE REACHES THE MOON, and only once: the smoke chain — 衣かつぎ steam → the rabbit's pyre → 叢雲 → incense → Fuji's undying smoke (the elixir and, burned with it, the emperor's poem), which touches the moon at 214.0.
THE 縁 MOTIF broken on its fifth note at the CLICK and completed sixty years later by the shakuhachi — the one left behind finishes the phrase.
INSECTS ARE THE EARTH'S HEARTBEAT: silent at the leap and under the cloud, returning one by one; the film ends on a single suzumushi.
PRETENDING NOT TO SEE: お月見泥棒 at 33.0 (たけ turns to the moon) is inherited at 197.5 (小夜 turns to the moon) — the fox is the thief the second time.

THE FOX WINDOW: たけ shows the child the moon's true face — enormous, blank, waiting — and the window opens into it (三 → 四); sixty years later the old hands show the old woman her own first night, still playing in colour (六).
THE SECOND TEACUP: two cups poured, one untouched with a tiny moon in it — rhyming with the ladle-moon of 三 and with the scroll 掬水月在手. Never explained.

THE 形見: Kaguya's letter asks that the robe she leaves be kept as a keepsake; on screen it is たけ's 波兎 haori, laid over the sleeping child, worn by her for sixty years (羽織 visually rhymes with 羽衣). 小夜's haiku 「形見着て」 in 七 answers the letter: she did what Kaguya asked.
THE HELD-BACK BELL: no 梵鐘 until dawn, and then only the three 捨て鐘 that precede 明け六つ — the hour itself is never struck; their hum is tuned to the note the shakuhachi finally supplies.

金木犀 florets (桂花 / 月中桂) drift through the first night — a wordless bridge for the Chinese viewer, alongside 掬水月在手, 邵雍's 月到天心処 behind Buson (the subtitle simply reads 月到天心) and Bai Juyi's couplet, which the Chinese viewer reads in the 画賛 itself.

characters.name: たけ（祖母・Take）
characters.look: Bent, small 銀鼠 bun with a 煤竹 comb; kimono 紺 with 鼠 stripes, 黄土 obi, a subdued 海老茶 obijime (right for her age); the 波兎 haori (藍 ground, 胡粉 rabbits leaping over seigaiha waves). Never a face beyond a closed-eye line in profile.
characters.build: CAST.elder (poses stand/kneel/weep/point) as a cut-out rig; her shadow is the same path filled 藍鼠.

characters.name: 小夜（Sayo）, 6
characters.look: 墨 okappa bob, 紺 kasuri kimono with 胡粉 flecks, a soft 紅絞りの兵児帯 (red shibori heko-obi tied in a loose bow at the back — everyday wear for a six-year-old at a Shōwa home tsukimi; no 帯揚げ). Back views, silhouettes, a tiny figure against the moon. Only in the 六 fox-window inset (gazeOut) does she turn: a 3-key silhouette swap back → profile → three-quarter with 0.25 s crossfades, the three-quarter face a flat 胡粉 oval under the okappa fringe with two 5 px 墨 Harunobu slit-eyes and no mouth.

characters.name: 小夜, 66
characters.look: Drawn on たけ's EXACT path and pose table (same silhouette, same haori), white bun. The audience must mistake her for たけ until the faded 退紅 strip of her old heko-obi gives her away (171.0) — no text on screen before then.
characters.build: CAST.elder, identical parameters to たけ — the reuse is the point of the film.

characters.name: 狐（the fox, witness）
characters.look: Almost never seen: two eye-glints in the susuki at moonrise (20–22, α 0.6), the Jataka fox with its fish on the moon's face (93.4–103), a 藍鼠 shadow on the closed shoji and a 墨 paw that steals a dango (195.0–196.2), a small sitting silhouette in the dawn susuki (206–236). The only creature present on both nights, sixty years apart.
characters.build: CAST.fox (sit/walk) as a 墨 silhouette; glints are two 胡粉 points.

characters.name: 月の兎
characters.look: In the Jataka on the moon's face (sumi silhouette); then the maria — a rabbit with pestle and mortar in 薄墨, settled from fourteen brush strokes of smoke.
characters.build: CAST.rabbit (hop/leap/pound) silhouettes clipped to the disc.

moon_clock.rule: The moon is ONE unbroken celestial arc for the whole film, never cut, never re-printed, never drawn twice in one frame. Its angle φ(t) is a monotone cubic (PCHIP, Fritsch–Carlson) through the keypoints and HELD — not extrapolated — outside them: φ = −0.22 for t ≤ 14 (so 序's dry disc is exactly 一's first moon) and φ = π for t ≥ 222.6. Each master shot projects φ with its own mapping, so the moon may sit in different screen places in different shots but its sky position, size law and colour are continuous. Rise (t 16) → culmination inside the round window (t 140.0) takes 124 s; culmination → set behind Fuji's summit (t 222.6) takes only 82.6 s: the moon falls faster in old age (time dilation, cf. 「月はやし」). The keypoint [148, 1.64] lets the moon linger near the window's centre while she climbs (≤ 31 px off-centre through her entry at 148.4) and fall faster once she is gone.

mappings.A: x = 960 − 800·cosφ ; y = 700 − 560·sinφ ; r = 72 + 38·(1 − sinφ)²  (horizon illusion: r≈128 at 序, 72 at culmination). The hole is the disc ∩ skyMask(A): at x 0–760 the sky continues behind the susuki down to the far pond bank y 820 (far hills only at x 760–1500), so the rising moon sits in sky with the far and mid susuki plumes printed over it and the near live susuki drawn on top. Checkpoints: 序 (t ≤ 14) (179,822) r 128 — a dry half-disc x 51–307, y 694–820; 16 (168,778) r 121; 21 (160,696) r 110 (poster); 35 (200,526) r 90; 40 (223,482) r 86; after the 四 tilt 111 (703,170) r 72 → 118 (762,158); 六 160 (1264,182) r 72 → 190 (1581,347) r 77.
mappings.A_prime: Moon off-frame (upper right); only its light direction matters: shadows fall to the lower left.
mappings.B: Moon glow behind the shoji paper: centre x = 960 − 420·cosφ, y = 960 − 810·sinφ, radial bokashi r 220. The disc itself (r 64) is visible only through the round window (centre (960,150), r 110; the disc is fully inside while its centre is ≤ 46 px off): fully inside t 131–150, exactly centred at 140.0 (16.5 px right at 145, 24 at 147, 29 at 148, 31 at 148.4, 44 at 150); from 151 its right rim is cut by the window's edge (79 px off at 153, 106 at 155).
mappings.C: Reflection only (art-directed): ellipse rx 70 ry 52 at (1000,600) in the tsukubai (Shot C is more overhead, so the eclipse ring lands on the basin rim).
mappings.D: Looking straight up: fixed at (960,430), r 260, 月暈 halo ring r 420. During the 四 tilt (108.0–111.0) the moon is drawn ONCE, on top of both masters: e = inOutSine((t−108)/3); centre = lerp((960,430),(703,170),e); r = lerp(260,72.1,e); maria scaled with the disc; halo α × (1−e). From 111.0 mapping A.
mappings.E: Dawn (art-directed, linear in t, no easing — the moon must never appear to drop): r 48, velocity (5,16) px/s. (1140,202) at 206.0 → (1180,330) at 214.0 (lower rim y 378 meets the smoke tip on the axis x 1180) → rim resting on the summit plateau ≈216.6 (パール富士) → half sunk (1210,426) at 220.0 → hidden (1223,468) behind the plateau at 222.6, just as the warm plates lift.

moon_clock.colour: φ < 0.3: 山吹 glaze α = 0.55·(1 − sinφ) over the bare paper; 0.3–2.7: bare 生成 with a 月白 glaze α 0.2; φ > 2.7: 銀鼠 glaze rising to α 0.5, kira fading.
moon_clock.rendering: moonHole = disc ∩ skyMask(shot): a destination-out hole through the sky plates only, down to the washi. Whatever the shot places in front of the sky — far/mid susuki plume silhouettes, hills, kasumi bands, the reed lattice of the round window, Fuji's summit — prints over the moon; near live susuki draws on top. A kira band (soft 胡粉 'lighter' stripe, 30 px, 30°) sweeps the disc every 7 s (on t_abs). The face is BLANK until t 106.0; from then on the rabbit's maria (墨 α 0.22, a separate 'rabbit plate' R) are the only ink ever laid on the moon. In the 後摺 the disc is exempt from yellowing and wear: it is the one fresh thing in the late impression. After the final unprinting it survives as a karazuri (blind-embossed) circle carrying the rabbit's faint carbon (α 0.10).
moon_clock.law_of_contact: Nothing touches the moon except once: Fuji's smoke at t 214.0, after which the moon slides down the thread (烟中月) until it is hidden at 222.6. Clouds may pass in front of it; the incense (七) points at it and stops 114–224 px short.

plates.state: Every plate is drawn from its per-shot cache with a per-t (dx, dy, alpha). The moon's disc is cut out of every plate (destination-out). One table drives: the printing in 序, the tears and CLICK in 五, the 後摺 state and its jolt in 六, and the unprinting in 結.
plates.shozuri: 初摺 (first impression, t 0–160): all plates on, registration within ±0.5 px, crisp bokashi, fresh pigments, 生成 paper.
plates.atozuri: 後摺 (late impression, t 160–236): P2 alpha 0 (except the single hand-applied 鴇/退紅 spot: the strip of faded heko-obi tying the susuki); P6 printed flat with NO bokashi and NO ichimonji at α 0.55 and offset (+5,−3); P5 offset (+5,−3); K with seeded dash-gaps (≤ 8% of length) and a few cracks; stronger goma-zuri speckle; paper 生成 × 鳥の子 multiply + ~60 foxing dots (煤竹 α 0.12–0.25). Restraint: it must read as an old print, not a broken render.
plates.jolt: t 160.0–160.6: each plate performs a damped oscillation of amplitude 4–8 px (seeded direction, 3 cycles), P2 rises 4 px as its alpha falls to 0, key-line gaps and yellowing ramp 0→1.
plates.tears: t 140.0–147.8: offsets P1 (0,+12), P2 (+10,+4), P5 (−12,−6), P6 (+6,−10), P7 (−4,+8), P4 (±3 only, so the climbing shadow stays legible), K holds at (0,0). Each is multiplied by ramp(140→142)·sin(2π(t−140)/3.1 + 1.3·i). The misaligned holes give the moon chromatic fringes (藍 on the left, 山吹 on the right, 1–4 px).
plates.click: t 147.8: every plate snaps to (0,0) within 60 ms, no overshoot. Perfect register = the loss of feeling.
plates.unprint: t 222.0–228.0, in approximately the order ukiyo-e pigments fade — plant dyes first, mineral pigments later, carbon never: D + P2 (鴇/東雲 and any plant-dye pinks and yellows: 紅, 萩, 山吹) 222.0–223.5 → P5 + P6 (the blues) 223.5–225.0 → P1 + P3 + P4 (黄土, 松葉, 尾花, 鼠, 銀鼠; 朱, a stable mineral, would belong here — the 後摺 has none left) 225.0–226.5 → K last 226.5–228.0 (carbon never fades). Each group slips 2–4 px out of register and rises 4 px as its alpha falls to 0. The rabbit plate R stays at α 0.10.

sound_bible.scale: 都節 (miyako-bushi / in) on D: D–E♭–G–A–B♭. Koto in 平調子 on D.
sound_bible.en_motif: The 縁 motif, A4–B♭4–D5–E♭5–D5 (the E♭ reached by oshide press from D). Stated WHOLE only once, at moonrise (t 16.5–19.9). During the climb (140–147.8) the koto forgets it in four passes; it breaks off at the CLICK on the rest where the fifth note (D5, 'home') should fall. At 210.5 the koto offers the first four notes again; at 214.0 the SHAKUHACHI — the voice of the one left behind — plays the missing D5 as the smoke touches the moon, and the dawn bell's hum (tuned to D) sustains it.
sound_bible.earth_heartbeat: Insects are mortal life. Suzumushi ('rīn': 4.2–4.6 kHz sine carriers, 30–40 Hz AM trill) and matsumushi ('chin-chirorin', ≈3.5 kHz, 3-note pattern). They stop for 1.2 s at the rabbit's leap (99.0–100.2), thin out as heaven arrives (132–140), vanish entirely under the cloud (148.0–152.0, absolute silence) and return one at a time (156.6, 158.2). In the 後摺 only three remain, then two, then one. The last sound of the film is a single suzumushi (233.0).
sound_bible.heaven: Shō aitake cluster A4 B4 E5 F♯5 A5 B5 (no semitones: heaven has none), breath-swelled; kagura-suzu shimmer (inharmonic 3–9 kHz); the fox-window glass cluster A6 B6 E7.
sound_bible.punctuation: Sōzu KON (200 Hz sine thump + wood click, big room reverb) at 40.0 (cut to the theatre), 160.0 (sixty years pass) and 232.5 (the water has returned); a dry sōzu in 六 and a dew 'plink' at 201.5. The kentō CLICK (1.2 kHz woodblock tick, 12 ms + 180 Hz thunk) is taught in 序 as the sound of a block landing in register and returns once, at 147.8, as the sound of forgetting. The 梵鐘 is WITHHELD for the whole film until dawn: three strokes at 215, 220, 225 — the 捨て鐘 that precede 明け六つ (the hour's own six strokes are never heard; the film ends just before the hour) (additive inharmonic partials 0.5, 1, 1.18, 1.5, 2.0, 2.74, 3.76 over a D hum, one pair detuned 0.7 Hz for 唸り, 12 s decay).
sound_bible.instruments: Koto (Karplus-Strong; 後摺 = higher loss, shorter decays), shakuhachi (sine + band-passed breath, meri/kari bends, muraiki onsets), biwa (Karplus-Strong + sawari noise buzz) for the shadow-play, shō (additive cluster), kagura-suzu, soft taiko (55–90 Hz sine thumps), small 鏧 bowl (only at the rabbit's leap), wind in susuki (pink noise 0.8–2 kHz, seeded gusts), water (trickle, drops as gliding sine pings), geese (two-formant FM honks), paper (baren rub, brush swishes, peel swishes).
sound_bible.silences: 0–2 (paper), 99.0–100.2 (the leap: only the bowl), 148.0–152.0 (absolute: master gain 0), 234.2–236.0 (end).
sound_bible.scrubbing: Continuous beds read their parameters from t; discrete events come from a sorted event list and are rescheduled from the current t on every seek.

text_style.fonts: Japanese vertical (writing-mode: vertical-rl): Shippori Mincho B1 for poems and narration; Yuji Syuku (font 'brush') for the title column and for Kaguya's letter (kind 'letter'). Chinese: one small horizontal line in Noto Serif SC in the subtitle band y 960–1040, at most 5 characters per second of fully-visible subtitle time (≤ 22 characters for an 8 s cue); bridges for the Chinese viewer stay wordless — no glosses in the subtitles.
text_style.seals: Classical texts: a small 朱文 seal 「月」 (red characters on the paper ground, red outline). 小夜's haiku: a 白文 seal 「小夜」 (paper-white characters on red). Title: 「縁」 朱文, painted on canvas at the tanzaku's foot (1721,434)–(1749,462). From 160 on (the 後摺) every DOM seal is printed in faded 退紅 (#EAA79A) instead of 朱 — COLOUR STAYS ON EARTH — and the final haiku carries no seal, so the canvas stamp 朱 「忘れじ」 ≈90 px at (1300,820), t 230.0, is the first and only saturated red after 160.
text_style.rules: 11 text blocks in 236 s, ≈88 s on screen (37%). Never two on screen at once; ≥ 1.5 s between cues; every haiku/waka/kanshi on screen ≥ 8 s. No text at all from 131.5 to 160 (celestials, ribbon, climb, cloud, drain), from 160 to 173.6 ('she has come back' plays as pure image), and from 214.0 to 226.8 (the contact, the missing note, the bells, the moonset). Text reveal and fade are computed from t (engine TEXT.update), never CSS animation. 'ink': light = 胡粉 on dark grounds, dark = 墨 on paper. When a cue sits on a painted cartouche (短冊/色紙), the SCENE draws the cartouche panel on canvas for the cue's exact interval; the DOM draws only the characters.
text_style.positions: Engine positions (css/film.css): right / upper-right / left / upper-left / center; every cue here also gives explicit x,y (left/top of the text block in logical px) to land in the shot's text pocket. When x is given the block's left edge is exactly x — no centring transform.
engine_requirements: text.js DEFAULTS: waka {reveal 3.0, out 1.5, stagger 0.085}; kanshi {reveal 2.6, out 1.5, stagger 0.11} (the 2-column couplet writes like a haiku: fully written ≈2.5 s, ≈3.9 s fully legible in 8 s); letter {reveal 3.0, out 1.4, stagger 0.09, brush font, default 40 px, letter-spacing 0.12em}.
Seals by seal_style: 朱文 = paper ground, 朱 characters, 2 px inset 朱 outline; 白文 = 朱 ground, paper-white characters. Cues starting ≥ 160 add a 'seal-faded' class that swaps 朱 for 退紅 #EAA79A.

seal:false must reach text.js: tools/script-from-screenplay.js copies seal only when truthy, and text.js then defaults to 「月」. Pass `seal: false` through (used by the title and by 影ひとつ — a dry run of the generator confirms 影ひとつ currently loses it). The generator also drops `en`; pass it through for the title cue.
When cue.x != null set root.style.transform = 'none' (.pos-center's translateX(-50%) otherwise shifts an explicitly placed block).
Cue 'font' is a class token: use 'brush' (the letter previously carried the prose value 'Yuji Syuku (brush)', which would become a broken class name).
The title is a kind 'haiku' cue with font 'brush' and no seal; its 短冊, 色紙 「十五夜摺」 and 縁 seal are painted on canvas by 序 and carried by 一 until 16.0.

MOON: φ held at −0.22 for t ≤ 14 and at π for t ≥ 222.6 (no linear extrapolation); keypoints per moon_clock (add [148,1.64]; [219,π] → [222.6,π]); MOON.E linear per mappings.E; one moon during the 四 tilt per mappings.D; the hole is disc ∩ skyMask(shot).
三's engine transition is a plain cut: the scene itself opens the fox window over Shot D's first frame (88.2–90.0).

segments.summary: The film is pulled like a woodblock print. Blank washi; a baren spirals out from the thatched house and reveals Shot A in sumi only; the colour blocks drop in one by one, each landing a few px out of register and settling with a wooden kentō click. One half-disc behind the susuki at the far left stays dry and glows 山吹: the moon exists before the world is printed. The title writes itself on a painted tanzaku — a sentence that stops halfway — while 十五夜摺 prints in the 色紙 beside it.
segments.time_of_night: dusk before moonrise (宵, ≈17:50 on 十五夜)

moon.phase_note: full (十五夜) but not yet risen: only a dry, unprinted half-disc (x 51–307, y 694–820 — the disc ∩ Shot A's sky mask; the far and mid susuki plumes print over it) and a 山吹 glow bokashi behind the susuki. φ is held at −0.22 for t ≤ 14, so this is exactly 一's first moon.
moon.motion: none; the glow breathes ±6% on a 7 s period (on t_abs) from 6s [6]

layers.name: washi
layers.description: Blank 生成 paper, full frame (the engine adds fibres and mottling). This scene adds a 40 px ragged deckle at all four edges and the 見当: a karazuri L-mark (鉤見当) at (1840,1040), arms 46 px, drawn as a 1 px 胡粉 highlight above-left and a 1 px 墨 α 0.12 shadow below-right.
layers.motion: 0.8s [0.8] the notch catches raking light (highlight α 0.2→0.6→0.35 over 1.2 s). Deckle visible to 6s [6], fading into the normal frame by 9s [9].

layers.name: key block (墨)
layers.description: The complete Shot A line-work in 墨 α 0.85: house, thatch hatching, shoji kumiko, engawa, pond rim, sōzu, susuki plume lines, Fuji contour, 萩 branch. No fills.
layers.motion: 2s [2]–6s [6] revealed through a baren mask: an Archimedean spiral centred on the house (1180,560), stroke width 150 px, reach r(t) = 1300·inOutSine((t−2)/4); goma-zuri speckle (seeded 1–2 px gaps, 6%) where the spiral overlaps itself.

layers.name: colour plates
layers.description: Shot A's plates in printing order (see plates): P1 黄土, P2 warm (紅/萩/山吹), P3 松葉+尾花, P4 greys, P5 藍 pond, P6 ベロ藍 sky with ichimonji and a 山吹 horizon bokashi at x 0–760, y 600–820 (α 0→0.25 downward), P7 胡粉/月白, P8 kira.
layers.motion: Plate i lands at 6s [6] + 0.6·i (i = 0…7: 6.0, 6.6, 7.2, 7.8, 8.4, 9.0, 9.6, 10.2): α 0→1 in 0.12 s from a seeded offset of 4–6 px, easing to (0,0) with outCubic over 0.45 s; the kentō click sounds as it touches. P6's ichimonji band is wiped left→right 9s [9.0]–9.6s [9.6].

layers.name: the moon before the moon
layers.description: A dry unprinted half-disc: moonHole = disc (179,822) r 128 ∩ skyMask(A) — x 51–307, y 694–820 — cut out of the sky plates (destination-out); the far and mid susuki plume silhouettes and the low kasumi print over it. Behind the susuki a 山吹 glow bokashi: radial, α 0.35 at r 60 → 0 at r 300, centred (180,770).
layers.motion: A faint glow (×0.3) is there from 2s [2] as the spiral passes; the dry disc reads as a hole when the first plate lands 6s [6] — colour arrives everywhere except here. Glow breathes ±6% (7 s, on t_abs).

layers.name: near susuki
layers.description: The live near-susuki layer of Shot A (≈150 plumes).
layers.motion: Frozen until 13s [13]; the first gust leans the plumes 4° and they begin their normal sway: the print starts to breathe. Sway and gusts read t_abs, so 一 continues this gust without a restart.

layers.name: title panels (canvas)
layers.description: The 短冊 panel for the title: x 1680–1790, y 60–470, 生成 ground with a 1.5 px 紅 border and faint 山吹 砂子 specks; the DOM writes only the single column 月の出でたらむ夜は (Yuji Syuku 36 px, y 74–443). The scene paints: the 縁 seal (朱文, 28 px) at (1721,434)–(1749,462) at the tanzaku's foot, and the square 色紙 x 1560–1660, y 60–160 carrying 「十五夜摺」 as a 2×2 block (right column 十五, left column 夜摺; Yuji Syuku 32 px, 墨) centred (1610,110).
layers.motion: Panels, seal and 十五夜摺 print in with P2 6.6s [6.6] — they are part of the print. They outlive 序: 一 keeps drawing them unchanged and fades them 14.4–16.0 together with the DOM title's fade-out (1.6 s ending at 16.0).

beats.desc: Blank washi. Paper room tone only.
The 見当 notch catches the light.
The baren begins: sumi lines spiral out from the house; a faint warmth behind the far-left susuki.
The first colour block (黄土) lands 5 px out of register and settles — click. One half-disc behind the susuki stays dry: the moon's place.
The warm block lands: the tanzaku, the 色紙 with 十五夜摺 and the 縁 seal print in.
The title begins to write itself in one brushed column.
The ベロ藍 sky lands; the ichimonji band is wiped across the top (9.0–9.6).
Mica lands; the print sparkles faintly.
The first suzumushi, far away.
The first gust in the susuki: the print is alive.

text_cues.reading: つきのいでたらむよは
text_cues.source: Title taken from Kaguya-hime's farewell letter in 『竹取物語』 (「月の出でたらむ夜は、見おこせたまへ」), deliberately stopped halfway.
text_cues.zh: 月出之夜 · 十五夜摺
text_cues.en: On Nights When the Moon Comes Out — A Fifteenth-Night Impression
text_cues.note: Title. One brushed column (9 × 36 × 1.14 ≈ 369 px: y 74–443) on the 短冊 the scene paints at x 1680–1790, y 60–470. 十五夜摺 (2×2 in the 色紙) and the 縁 seal are painted on canvas, not DOM. kind 'haiku', so zh and en go to the subtitle band (no .title-sub overflow). The cue crosses the 序→一 hand-off and ends at 16.0 (fade 14.4–16.0): ≈4 s fully legible. The sentence is completed on screen at 122.5 s by the letter.

segments.negative_space: Upper-right x 1540–1830, y 50–480 (title tanzaku + 色紙) is flat ベロ藍 sky only, through 16.0; Fuji's peak (1720,500) sits just below it. The dry moon half-circle (x 51–307, y 694–820) must never be covered by anything but the susuki plumes and the low kasumi. Subtitle band y 960–1040 = pond: calm.
segments.audio: 0–2: near silence (paper room tone, brown noise −50 dB). 2.0–6.0: baren rub — band-passed brown noise 300–1200 Hz whose gain follows the spiral's speed, in 0.7 s circular strokes. 6.0–10.2: eight kentō clicks, one per plate at 6.0, 6.6, 7.2, 7.8, 8.4, 9.0, 9.6, 10.2 (1.2 kHz woodblock tick, 12 ms, plus a soft 180 Hz thunk). This exact click returns at 147.8 as the sound of forgetting, so it must be clean and memorable. 7.0: one koto 引き色 — D4 plucked, then pulled ~40 cents flat — as the title lands. 12.0: first suzumushi (single far voice). 13.0: first susuki gust (pink noise 0.8–2 kHz swell).
segments.transition_out: Seamless hand-off (0 s): the last frame of 序 is Shot A 初摺 fully printed and 一 begins on the identical frame — the same moon (φ held at −0.22 → (179,822) r 128) and the same gust (sway on t_abs). The title and its painted panels carry across the cut and fade together 14.4–16.0.
segments.hero_image: 4.2s [4.2] — Shot A half-born: sumi lines have spiralled out from the thatched house across half the sheet; the rest is blank washi with its deckle and registration notch; behind the unprinted susuki lines at the far left a half-disc of paper glows faintly 山吹 — the moon before the world.
segments.simplification: Cache Shot A's key block and each colour plate once (they are reused by 一, 四 and 六). The reveal is a mask canvas (the spiral stroked with round caps, lineWidth 150) applied with destination-in; plate landings are drawImage with (dx,dy,alpha). No per-frame blur.

segments.summary: First impression. The dry half-disc that waited behind the susuki lifts: a huge 山吹 moon with a blank face; six-year-old 小夜, carrying susuki taller than herself, crosses the disc — the poster frame. Two eye-glints in the grass: the fox. She runs the pond rim (Bashō's 'all night long', as delight) while grandmother たけ builds the 三方: fifteen dango, one per koto pluck, stacked 9-4-2; 衣かつぎ steam for 芋名月; the autumn grasses in a jug; a few 金木犀 florets drift past. お月見泥棒: a small arm steals a dango and たけ turns to the moon and pretends not to see; the child climbs up beside her to eat it. たけ blows out the andon; the shoji turn moon-white; the theatre opens. KON.

moon.phase_note: full; blank uninked face; warm 山吹 glaze at the horizon cooling toward bare paper
moon.motion: Shot A mapping of φ(t), continuing 序's dry half-disc (179,822) r 128: it begins to lift 2s [16] (168,778) r 121; (160,711) r 111 6s [20]; poster (160,696) r 110 7s [21]; clears the far susuki top (y 620) ≈21s [35] at (200,526) r 90; (223,482) r 86 26s [40]. Glaze α 0.55·(1−sinφ).

layers.name: sky
layers.description: Ichimonji band y 0–130 in ベロ藍 + 墨 35% (solid to y 60, fading out by y 130); below, ベロ藍 → 紺 bokashi to y 420, flattening into 藍 at the horizon y 620 and, at x 0–760, continuing down behind the susuki to the far pond bank y 820; a 山吹 horizon bokashi at the left (x 0–760, y 600–820, α 0→0.25 downward) — the glow of the rising moon.
layers.motion: Horizon glow fades 0.25→0.08 as the moon clears the susuki (16s [30]–26s [40]).

layers.name: moon
layers.description: Hole through all plates to 生成 paper; radius per mapping; 山吹 glaze; kira band sweeping the disc every 7 s. Face blank.
layers.motion: φ(t).

layers.name: far land
layers.description: Low 紺 hills y 580–640 at x 760–1500 only (no key line); at x 0–760 there are no hills — the sky runs down behind the susuki so the moon rises out of the grass. Fuji small, peak (1720,500), flanks reaching y 620 at x 1500 and 1940, flat ベロ藍 with a thin 胡粉 first-snow line 6–10 px under the peak, half-hidden by the kasumi.
layers.motion: static

layers.name: kasumi
layers.description: Suyari-gasumi bands (胡粉 α 0.55, rounded ends, soft upper edge): y 585–625 across x 280–1320 and x 1480–1920; y 780–805 across x 0–900.
layers.motion: drift +3 px/s

layers.name: house
layers.description: Thatch 黄土 with 尾花 highlights and 墨 hatching (ridge y 430, eaves y 560, x 900–1460); 墨 posts; four shoji x 980–1380, y 575–690, lit 山吹 by the andon inside, 墨 kumiko; engawa boards 煤竹 (黄土×墨) y 690–705, x 940–1420.
layers.motion: 23s [37] the shoji go 山吹 → 月白 over 1.2 s (andon blown out) and the warm spill on the engawa and near susuki fades with them.

layers.name: offerings
layers.description: On the engawa's left end: 三方 at (1000,690) (白木: 生成 with 黄土 edges, 墨 key, 26×14 px); fifteen dango as 胡粉 circles r 4 stacked 9-4-2; a 鼠 jug with susuki, 萩 (萩 dots), 女郎花 (山吹 dots) and 桔梗 (桔梗 stars); a dish of 衣かつぎ (尾花 ovals with 墨 tips) at (1030,690) with three steam ribbons (胡粉 α 0.35).
layers.motion: Dango appear one per koto pluck 8.4s [22.4]–15.4s [29.4] (nine at 0.45 s spacing, a breath, four, a breath, two). Steam from 15.5s [29.5]. 19s [33] the top dango vanishes (14 remain).

layers.name: figures
layers.description: たけ (CAST.elder, ≈52 px kneeling, profile): bent back, 銀鼠 bun, the 波兎 haori (藍, 3–4 胡粉 specks at this size). 小夜 (CAST.child, ≈62 px): 墨 okappa, 紺 kasuri, 紅絞り heko-obi as a 2–3 px accent (a soft bow at the back), carrying a susuki sheaf 120 px tall.
layers.motion: 小夜: 4s [18] emerges from the susuki at x 120; 7s [21] crosses the disc (feet (190,790), head at y 735 against the moon); 8s [22]–16s [30] runs the pond rim — far bank x 400→1300 at y 830, back along the near bank at y 1040, 0.8 s bob per stride, reflection bobbing below; 16.5s [30.5] sets the flowers in the jug; 18.8s [32.8] ducks below the engawa lip (1010,712) and her arm rises 19s [33]. たけ: kneels at (1060,690) building the stand from 8s [22]; 19.6s [33.6] turns her head to the moon (profile flips left) and holds it there; 22.5s [36.5] her silhouette crosses the lit paper to the andon; 23s [37] blows it out. 小夜: 20.2s [34.2] climbs onto the engawa and sits at (1022,690), back view, facing the lit shoji, eating the stolen dango; she stays there through the andon at 23s [37] (the 六 fox-window inset needs her here at t′ 34–40).

layers.name: susuki field
layers.description: Three parallax layers y 620–820, densest at x 0–760: far (cached, 鼠 plumes α 0.5), mid (尾花 plumes, 黄土 stems), near (live, ≈150 plumes: curved 松葉 stem + a 12-stroke feathery 尾花/胡粉 plume, 墨 key line on 30%). The plumes stand in silhouette against the rising disc. During 4s [18]–9s [23] (the poster frame) the near-susuki density over x 40–320, y 580–800 is ≤ 20% and plumes there stay below y 760, so the disc's upper two-thirds and the tiny child stay clean.
layers.motion: sway = shear sin(0.9·t_abs + 0.004x)·gust(t_abs); gusts 5.5s [19.5], 13s [27], 21s [35] — continuing 序's gust of 13.0 without a restart

layers.name: fox glints
layers.description: Two eye-glints in the susuki at (612,748) and (626,748): 胡粉 points r 1.6 with 山吹 halos r 4, at α 0.6 (never full). Nothing else of the fox.

layers.name: pond
layers.description: x 200–1500, y 820–1080: 藍 with ベロ藍 bokashi at the far edge; Hiroshige moon road — horizontal 胡粉 dashes (4–40 px × 2 px) stacked under the moon's x, shimmering on sin(y·k + t); 小夜's reflection (墨 α 0.35, broken by the dashes).
layers.motion: the road follows the moon's x and brightens as it rises

layers.name: sōzu & tsukubai
layers.description: Sōzu at (320,880): bamboo tube 松葉/尾花, 墨 nodes, pivot post; tsukubai stone (420,930) in 鼠.
layers.motion: The tube fills through the segment, tips 25.8s [39.8] and strikes the stone 26s [40] — the KON is the cut.

layers.name: 萩 branch
layers.description: Foreground frame across the top-left (x 0–380, y 0–260): tapered 墨 stems, 松葉 leaflets, 萩 blossom clusters.
layers.motion: ±2° sway, 11 s period

layers.name: 金木犀
layers.description: Three osmanthus florets (4-petal crosses, 4 px, 朱 with 山吹 centres).
layers.motion: drift from (300,120) down-right across the 萩 branch 10s [24]–18s [32] (seeded B.drift), gone by 20s [34]

layers.name: title panels (carried from 序)
layers.description: 序's tanzaku, 色紙 (十五夜摺) and 縁 seal, drawn unchanged from the cached 序 panel canvas.
layers.motion: 0s [14]–0.4s [14.4] hold; 0.4s [14.4]–2s [16] fade out with the DOM title (inSine); gone from 16.0.

beats.desc: The print breathes: wind, the insects gathering. The title still stands on its tanzaku.
The title and its painted panels begin to fade (gone at 16.0).
The dry half-disc that has waited behind the susuki since 序 begins to lift — huge, 山吹, blank. The 縁 motif sounds whole on the koto (16.5–19.9): the only complete statement in the film.
小夜 emerges from the susuki with a sheaf taller than herself.
Two eye-glints in the grass — the fox (α 0.6). A blink at 21.2; gone at 22.0.
POSTER FRAME: the tiny child silhouetted on the gold disc.
小夜 runs the pond rim; たけ begins the 三方.
Dango appear one per pluck: nine … four … two (to 29.4).
金木犀 florets drift across the 萩 branch.
衣かつぎ set down; steam rises (芋名月).
小夜 sets susuki, 萩, 女郎花 and 桔梗 in the jug.
お月見泥棒: a small arm from below the engawa takes the top dango. Fourteen remain.
たけ turns her face to the moon and pretends not to see.
小夜 climbs onto the engawa and sits beside her, back to us, eating.
The andon is blown out; the shoji turn from 山吹 to 月白; the moon is the only light.
A slow push toward the shoji (scale 1.00→1.06 about (1180,630)).
The sōzu tips.
KON — hard cut.

text_cues.reading: めいげつや　いけをめぐりて　よもすがら
text_cues.author: 芭蕉
text_cues.source: 松尾芭蕉　貞享三年（1686）八月十五夜、深川芭蕉庵の月見にて　『孤松』所収
text_cues.zh: 明月当空——绕着池塘走啊走，走了一整夜。
text_cues.note: On screen 小夜 is literally circling the pond: Bashō's delight. The poem's 'all night long' is the film's own time-scale (one night, twice).

segments.negative_space: Sky pocket x 500–860, y 60–580 (between the 萩 branch and the house) holds only flat bokashi for the haiku. The title region x 1540–1830, y 50–480 stays flat sky until 16.0. The rising moon at far left (x 40–320) must never be covered by text. Subtitle band y 960–1040 = pond: keep moon-road dashes sparse there (α ≤ 0.35).
segments.audio: Wind in the susuki (pink noise band-passed 0.8–2 kHz, gusts at 19.5, 27.0, 35.0). Insect chorus builds: suzumushi 1→8 voices by 30 s; matsumushi 3 voices from 24 s. Sōzu trickle (narrow-band noise). 16.5–19.9: the 縁 motif WHOLE on koto, rubato — A4 16.5 · B♭4 17.2 · D5 17.9 · E♭5 18.8 (oshide from D5) · D5 19.9, long decay. 22.4–29.4: fifteen koto plucks, one per dango — the counting melody in miyako-bushi: D4 E♭4 G4 A4 B♭4 A4 G4 E♭4 D4 | G4 A4 B♭4 D5 | E♭5 D5. 33.0: paper rustle; 33.6: a single koto harmonic (the grandmother's complicity — this exact harmonic returns at 197.5). 37.0: a breath puff (0.3 s) and the andon flame gutter. 40.0: sōzu KON — 200 Hz sine thump + wooden click, long room reverb; every bed cuts with it.
segments.transition_out: Hard cut on the KON at 40.0 (0 s) to Shot B interior; the last 2 s push slowly toward the darkened shoji so the cut feels like stepping inside.
segments.hero_image: 7s [21] — a vast 山吹 moon cut by silhouetted susuki plumes; across its lower third a tiny black child carries an over-tall sheaf of susuki; a 萩 branch hangs in from the top-left under a ベロ藍 ichimonji band (homage: 武蔵野図屏風; 芳年『月百姿』).
segments.simplification: Far/mid susuki, hills, Fuji, house and pond body come from the cached Shot A plates; only the near susuki, figures, dango, steam, glints and moon road animate. Figures are CAST.elder / CAST.child at small scale; dango are circles; the 9-4-2 stack is a fixed coordinate list revealed by count(t).

segments.summary: Inside, the andon out. Four moon-white shoji are the screen and the rising moon is the lantern. On the engawa outside, たけ holds paper cut-outs in the moonlight; inside, 小夜 kneels with her back to us and watches the Tale of the Bamboo Cutter play across the panels right to left, like an emaki. The shining culm is a slit in the paper; the princess is a hole in the shape of a girl — light is made of absence. One continuous morph grows her from a three-inch child into a woman with floor-length hair, and たけ's hand carries her across to the first panel. Under the real glow she raises her sleeve to her face; 小夜 looks up toward the round window; and たけ lifts a paper moon until it eclipses the real one — 'looking at the moon's face is forbidden'. The camera pushes into the ring of light.

beats.desc: Cut in on the KON. The shoji are cold 月白; the insects are muffled by the walls.
たけ's shadow lifts three paper culms into panel 4: a bamboo grove in sharp shadow. The biwa opens the tale.
The bamboo-cutter puppet (60 px) walks in along the bottom rail of panel 4.
One culm shines: a slit in the puppet lets the moonlight through — a 胡粉 point with kira.
The glowing culm's slit slowly widens; inside sits a three-inch girl-shaped hole of light, 26 px tall (「筒の中光りたり…三寸ばかりなる人、いとうつくしうてゐたり」 — no axe: the tale has none).
たけ's hand-shadow carries her into panel 3. ONE CONTINUOUS MORPH (50.5–54.5): child → girl → young woman with hair to the floor, always a hole of light in a dark oval cut-out.
Hold on the grown Kaguya while たけ's hand-shadow carries her across panel 2 toward panel 1; a single koto D4 (55.5).
Panel 1, under the real glow: Kaguya — light in the shape of a woman on a cut-out engawa — raises her sleeve to her face (1.5 s).
In the foreground 小夜 tilts her head up toward the round window.
The whisper appears: 「月の顔見るは、忌むこと」.
たけ raises a paper-cut full moon on a stick; its dark shadow slides in from the right over the real glow. 小夜 lowers her head.
Alignment: a black disc ringed with light — an eclipse made by a grandmother's hand. Held (63.0–64.0); a low koto D2 rings.
Push-in on the ring (scale 1.00→1.50, its centre travelling to (960,610)) to land the match-cut.

segments.simplification: Every shadow is one flat 藍鼠 fill (multiply); penumbra = 2–3 offset low-alpha passes, not blur. Puppets are simple paths; the negative puppet is one path filled evenodd. The growth morph = three authored silhouettes with equal vertex counts (96), lerped. Base outlines from CAST.okina, CAST.kaguya ('weep') and CAST.elder. The palanquin is cut (see spares: きと影になりぬ).

segments.summary: At the tsukubai the child grabs the moon in the water and it shatters into mica. The ripples die; the moon returns, untouched. たけ's ladle lifts a tiny moon and tips it into the child's cupped hands; the moon leaks away between her fingers until her hands are dark and empty — her first lesson in transience, which she will write down sixty years later. Only insects. Then たけ's old hands glide in, already joined in the fox window: inside the diamond is the moon itself, enormous and blank — and the window opens until the sky is all there is.

beats.desc: Cut in on the stone rim: the reflected moon whole in dark, still water. A bead swells at the spout tip.
Small hands plunge in.
The moon shatters into some forty mica shards; the rings race outward.
The hands come up empty and dripping, bright beads falling.
The ripples die away; the shards regather (τ 0.5); by 71.8 the moon is whole again, untouched.
The first drop falls from the spout (then every 2.3 s). たけ's ladle enters from the top-right, dips (73.0), lifts (73.8): a tiny moon in its cup.
She tips it into 小夜's cupped hands.
The moon sits in the child's palms. A bead falls between her fingers every half-second; the moon shrinks with the water, r = 18·(1−(t−75.4)/6.8)^0.7.
The small hands tremble.
The last drop. The hands are dark and empty. Only insects (82.2–86.0).
小夜's haiku writes itself in the dark moss above the spout.
たけ's old hands glide in from the top-right, already joined in the fox window (狐の窓), and stop before the child's eye.
Inside the diamond: the moon itself, enormous and blank.
The window opens — hands and diamond grow ×12 until the sky is all there is (90.0).

segments.shot: D, then tilt down to A
segments.summary: Looking straight up: an enormous blank moon with a halo. On its paper face, in sumi, the Jataka plays: an old beggar sits by a fire the others have built — the only warm colour ever drawn inside the moon. A monkey brings fruit, a fox a fish; the rabbit comes with nothing and its ears droop. It looks up at us and leaps. The disc flashes white and every insect on earth stops for 1.2 s. The smoke drifts across the face in fourteen brush strokes and settles into a rabbit pounding with pestle and mortar: the maria are born, the only ink ever laid on the moon, and every moon afterwards keeps it. The pestle's ぺったん fades as we tilt down to earth — one moon travelling the whole way — where たけ gives her own dango to 小夜 and the child falls asleep in her lap.

A monkey enters from the left with fruit (92.0–93.4).
A fox enters from the right with a fish (93.4–94.8).
The rabbit hops in with nothing.
Its ears droop (held 1.2 s).
The rabbit looks up — out of the moon, at us (held 1.0 s).
It leaps in a parabola, apex 60 px above the flames, into the fire (98.9).
The disc flashes 胡粉 for 0.4 s. Every insect on earth stops (99.0–100.2).
The beggar rises; his outline turns to mica (帝釈天) and fades with the monkey and the fox (100–103).
Smoke rises from the fire in thin wisps across the blank face.
The insects return, one at a time.
The wisps begin to gather into brush strokes.
The maria are printed: a rabbit with pestle and mortar — the moon's only ink.

Tilt down to earth; the one moon travels with us, shrinking into the sky over the house; with every metre the pestle grows fainter until it cannot be heard (≈112).
The shō enters, pianissimo.
たけ gives 小夜 her own dango.
The child leans into her lap and falls asleep (115.5).

segments.summary: The climax. Inside again: the moon climbs into the round window. On the shoji, たけ's shadow lifts her haori against the light — for two seconds its rabbits-over-waves pattern shines through — and lays it over the sleeping child: the robe left behind as a keepsake, while Kaguya's letter completes the film's title. Then, without a word on screen, shadows cast by nothing: a cloud of celestials slides down the paper though the garden is empty, and a ribbon of light — the heavenly robe — unfurls down the central stile. At the moon's culmination her shadow peels off the paper, straightens out of old age and climbs the lattice rung by rung, while every colour plate drifts out of register like eyes filling with tears and the koto forgets its melody. She looks back once — though the robe should already have changed her heart. CLICK — perfect register, cold: she has forgotten. She enters the moon; a black cloud covers it; absolute silence. When it passes, only the child's shadow remains under the haori's, and the moon is sliding out of the window. Cut, in silence, to the engawa: たけ sits upright with her eyes closed; a wave drains her colour to moon-white while the haori and the child's red heko-obi stay bright. The child casts a shadow; the grandmother casts none. One cricket. Then another.

beats.desc: Through the mist wipe: Shot B. The glow has climbed to the top of the shoji. The shō, pianissimo.
The moon's rim enters the round window.
たけ's shadow slips off her haori. The letter begins to write itself, stroke by stroke.
She holds the haori up against the moon: for two seconds its rabbits and waves shine through onto the paper.
She lays it over the sleeping child; the shadows merge.
Stillness. Her hands in her lap. The moon is wholly inside the window by 131.

SHADOWS CAST BY NOTHING: a cloud with seven celestials and a canopied carriage slides down panels 2–3. The garden outside is empty; her real shadow does not move. The insects thin (8→3 voices by 138). No text from here to 160.
A ribbon of light unfurls down the central stile and reaches her (139.8).

CULMINATION: the moon exactly centred in the round window. Her shadow peels off the paper and stands; its back straightens. The colour plates begin to drift out of register — the room trembles like eyes filling with tears; the moon grows blue and gold fringes. The koto begins to forget.
She climbs the kumiko rung by rung; each cell flashes as she passes; her hair lengthens into Heian hair; the ribbon winds round her.
At the top, under the window, she looks back once — though the robe should already have changed her heart (「衣着せつる人は、心異になるなり」). One E♭ on the koto: the ache, for a single note.
CLICK. Perfect register, sharp and cold. The koto stops on the rest where the fifth note should be.
She enters the moon (kira pinpoint 148.4). A black cloud covers the window; the shoji go dark. ABSOLUTE SILENCE (148.0–152.0).
The cloud passes; a breath of wind returns.
The moon alone in the window, sliding out past its right edge. On the paper only the child's small shadow under the haori's. Her seated shadow is gone.
Hard cut, in silence, to Shot A′ outside: たけ upright, eyes closed; the child asleep in her lap.
Her colour drains downward like moonlight — to 胡粉 and 銀鼠 — while the haori and the red heko-obi stay bright (to 157.8).
One suzumushi. The child casts a shadow; the grandmother casts none.
Stillness (157.8–160.0): a second suzumushi (158.2); the sōzu trickle (159.2).
KON.

segments.shot: A (後摺), A′ inserts, 月に雁 crop
segments.summary: The same garden pulled sixty years later from the worn blocks: no warm colours, a flat sky without bokashi, broken key lines, drifted registration, yellowed and foxed paper. Reeds have taken half the pond, the sōzu is dry, one shoji is torn. Only the moon is fresh. A bent figure in the rabbit-and-wave haori sits on the engawa — drawn on たけ's exact path — so for a moment we believe she has come back; no words interrupt the belief. She stacks fifteen dango to a koto that has lost some of its notes; she pours two cups of tea, and one stays untouched with a tiny moon in it. A faded pink strip ties the susuki — torn from the child's red heko-obi. It is 小夜. A tall 月に雁 print: three geese cross the moon, the third lagging, with Bai Juyi's Mid-Autumn couplet as its inscription. Then her old hands rise into frame already joined in the fox window, and inside it the first impression is still playing — the warm andon, her grandmother, the little girl, who turns and looks out across sixty years. The hands tremble and come down.

segments.summary: The room is empty: no andon, no scroll — only a darker, unfaded rectangle where the scroll hung for decades. Through a torn panel a coin of moonlight falls on the tatami; through the open panel the moon hangs low and pale. 小夜 sits outside with her back to us and lights incense: a straight thread of smoke that points at the moon and stops short of it. She dozes. Two eye-glints peek round the stile and a fox's shadow rises on the paper of the closed panel; a paw takes the top dango. She wakes, sees, and — exactly as たけ did — turns her face to the moon and pretends not to see. Her haiku writes itself on the dark wall where Kaguya's letter once appeared: 形見着て.

小夜 lights incense; a thread of smoke rises straight at x 1180, pointing at the moon.
She dozes; her head nods twice.

She wakes, turns to the stand, and sees.
She turns her face to the moon and pretends not to see — たけ's gesture, inherited. The tilt of her head suggests a smile.

segments.summary: Dawn. Fuji from afar; the tiny house, one figure, the fox sitting in the susuki. The pale moon comes down toward the summit at a steady pace as a thread of smoke rises from the crater — the undying smoke of the burned elixir, burned with the emperor's poem. At 214.0 the smoke touches the moon's rim: the only contact between earth and moon in the whole film, the emperor's poem reaching her at last. The shakuhachi, voice of the one left behind, finally plays the missing fifth note, and the first bell of dawn — held back all night — sustains it. The moon slides down the thread (烟中月), rests on the summit and sinks behind it. 小夜's long dawn shadow reaches across the susuki toward where たけ went. Then the print unprints itself in approximately the order in which pigments fade — the plant-dye pinks and the dawn first, then the blues, then earths and greys, sumi last — until only blank washi remains, the registration notch, and a moon embossed in the paper carrying nothing but the rabbit's faint carbon. Her last haiku writes itself beside it. A red seal: 忘れじ — I will not forget.
segments.time_of_night: dawn, moonset (just before 明け六つ)

beats.desc: Match-cut: the incense line continues as Fuji's snow gully and smoke thread on the axis x 1180. 東雲 rises at the left. The tiny house, one figure, the fox in the susuki. The moon is already coming down, steadily.
The tale's last sentence writes itself: その煙、いまだ雲の中へ立ち昇るとぞ、言ひ伝へたる。
A thin koto offers the first four notes of the 縁 motif — A, B♭, D, E♭ — and waits.

The smoke touches the moon's lower rim — the only contact between earth and moon in the film, the emperor's burned poem reaching her; a kira flash runs round the rim. The SHAKUHACHI plays the missing D. No text until 226.8.
The first bell of dawn — the first of the three 捨て鐘 before 明け六つ — its hum tuned to D, sustains the note. 小夜's long dawn shadow is revealed from her feet toward the mountain.
The fox turns its head toward the peak.
Pearl Fuji: the moon rests on the summit, the smoke thread across its face.
Second bell. The moon is half sunk behind the summit.
The unprinting begins: the dawn and the plant pinks first … blues … earths … sumi last (228.0).
The moon has gone behind the mountain; the smoke goes on rising into an empty sky.
Third bell.
As the key block lifts, 小夜's last haiku writes itself beside the emerging embossed moon — the only new ink.
Blank washi, the registration notch, and a moon embossed in the paper with the rabbit's faint carbon.
A 朱 seal 「忘れじ」 is stamped — a soft taiko thud.
A last sōzu KON: the water has returned.
One suzumushi. The colophon. Silence to the end (236.0).

ja: その煙、いまだ雲の中へ
立ち昇るとぞ、言ひ伝へたる。
text_cues.reading: そのけぶり、いまだくものなかへ　たちのぼるとぞ、いいつたえたる。
text_cues.author: 竹取物語
text_cues.zh: 据说，那烟至今仍向云中升腾。
text_cues.note: The tale's last sentence, placed while the smoke climbs toward the moon; it has faded by the contact (214.0). The tale's own etymology for 富士 is 士に富む (many soldiers climbed the mountain); the 不死 wordplay works only in Japanese (ふじ / ふし) and is noted in the credits, never in a subtitle. Seal in faded 退紅.

text_cues.reading: かげひとつ　こうしをのぼる　りょうやかな
text_cues.author: 小夜
text_cues.zh: 一道影子，攀上窗格——好一个良宵。
text_cues.note: Her poem about that night; the film ends in her voice. Kigo 良夜 (仲秋). 格子 instead of 障子 avoids a winter-kigo 季重なり. It writes itself as the key block lifts (226.5–228) — the only new ink — right of the embossed moon (block ≈ x 1180–1452, y 170–725, clear of the moon x 810–1110). dur runs past 236.0, so its fade (236.0–237.6) is never seen: it stays to the last frame. No seal: 忘れじ (230.0) is the only red on the last paper.

segments.negative_space: Upper-left x 100–520, y 50–470 (pale sky above the 東雲) for the tale's last sentence (207.3–214.0). No text 214.0–226.8: the contact, the missing note, the bells, the moonset and the start of the unprinting. After the unprinting, the space right of the embossed moon x 1180–1460, y 150–780 for the final haiku, with the seal 忘れじ at (1300,820). Keep the moon's circle (x 810–1110, y 210–510) and the notch clear. Subtitle band y 960–1040: susuki, then bare paper.
segments.audio: Dawn pine-wind (soft low-passed noise); insects down to two voices. 210.5: thin koto (damped 後摺 decay) A4 · B♭4 · D5 · E♭5 — then the rest, waiting. 214.0: SHAKUHACHI D5, the missing fifth note: breathy muraiki onset, meri from C♯ up to D, then pure, held 6 s. 215.0 / 220.0 / 225.0: 梵鐘, the three 捨て鐘 that precede 明け六つ (the hour itself is never struck) — inharmonic partials over a D hum (D3 146.8 Hz), one pair detuned 0.7 Hz for 唸り, 12 s decay; the first stroke's hum sustains the shakuhachi's D. 222.0–228.0: four soft paper-peel swishes as the plate groups lift. 230.0: the seal — soft taiko thud (55 Hz sine + felt click) and a paper press. 232.5: sōzu KON (the water has returned). 233.0: one suzumushi 'rīn' (1.2 s). 234.2–236.0: silence.
segments.transition_out: End of film at 236.0: hold on blank washi — the embossed moon, the haiku, the seal, the notch, the colophon — in silence; the engine's end card follows. No fade to black: the film ends on paper.
segments.hero_image: 10.6s [216.6] — pearl Fuji at dawn: a pale moon resting on the snow-capped summit, a single thread of smoke rising across its face; 東雲 pink along the left horizon; far below, a tiny thatched house, a small fox in the susuki and one long shadow reaching toward the mountain (homage: 北斎『富嶽三十六景』; 芳年『月百姿』「烟中月」). Final frame 26s [232]: blank washi, an embossed moon with a faint rabbit, a vertical haiku and a red seal 忘れじ.
segments.simplification: Fuji is one polygon plus a snow polygon and the gully; the smoke is one tapered Bézier with glyphs; the moon is linear in t; the unprinting is the shared per-plate alpha table (序's printing machinery run backwards); the karazuri moon is two 2 px arcs and a paper sheen; the seal is B.seal; the colophon is one ctx.fillText in the loaded mincho.

ending: The film ends on paper, not on black. After Fuji's smoke — the burned elixir and the emperor's poem — touches the moon (214.0) and the shakuhachi supplies the missing note under the first dawn bell, the moon slides down the thread and sinks behind the summit (222.6), and the whole print lifts away in approximately the order in which ukiyo-e pigments fade — the plant-dye pinks and the dawn first, then the blues, then the earths and greys, and the carbon key block last (222–228). What remains is blank washi with its registration notch and, at the place of culmination, a moon embossed into the paper without ink, still carrying the rabbit's faint smoke — the one thing that was given to the moon and kept. 小夜's haiku 「影ひとつ格子をのぼる良夜かな」 writes itself beside it (226.8), the only new ink, unsealed; a red seal 「忘れじ」 (I will not forget) — the survivor's answer to the robe that erases grief, and the first fresh red since the grandmother's night — is pressed with a soft thud (230.0). A last sōzu KON: the water has returned to the dry bamboo. One suzumushi. A tiny colophon 「原典　竹取物語・今昔物語集」. Silence to 236.0.

fact_check: 『竹取物語』 quotations are locked to 新編日本古典文学全集 (流布本 school text); the wording and historical kana of the letter 「脱ぎおく衣を形見と見たまへ。月の出でたらむ夜は、見おこせたまへ」, the closing line 「その煙、いまだ雲の中へたち昇るとぞ、言ひ伝へたる」, 「月の顔見るは、忌むこと」 (said by ある人) and the two spare waka were checked; the displayed ja keeps historical kana, every 'reading' field is in modern kana (現代仮名遣い).

『今昔物語集』巻五第十三: 「万の人、月を見む毎に、此の兎の事思ひいだすべし」 comes at the end of the tale, right after the explanation that the cloud-like marks on the moon are the smoke of the rabbit's burning; the tale's closing formula follows it, so it is not the literal last sentence (結句). The manuscript reads 思出スベシ: the okurigana ス marks transitive いだす, so it is normalised 思ひいだすべし, not 思ひ出づべし. Text locked to 新日本古典文学大系33『今昔物語集 一』 (or 日本古典文学大系22); 新編日本古典文学全集 contains only 巻11–31.
芭蕉「名月や池をめぐりて夜もすがら」: 貞享三年（1686）八月十五夜、深川芭蕉庵の月見、『孤松』所収.
蕪村「月天心貧しき町を通りけり」: 明和五年（1768）; 月天心 after 邵雍《清夜吟》「月到天心処、風来水面時」. The Chinese subtitle reads 月到天心 with no gloss and no added adverb.

白居易 couplet: from 「八月十五日夜禁中独直対月憶元九」; collected in 『和漢朗詠集』 under 十五夜; recited by Genji in 『源氏物語』須磨. The Chinese subtitle carries only the attribution; the 故人 double sense (old friend in Chinese, the departed in modern Japanese) is kept to the treatment and the credits' note.

富士 naming: the tale itself derives 富士 from the many soldiers (士に富む) who climbed; 不死 is the celebrated wordplay, which works only in Japanese (ふじ / ふし, both ふし in historical kana) — in Mandarin 富士 fùshì and 不死 bùsǐ do not sound alike. The note sits in the credits, never in a subtitle, and the screenplay never claims the text says 不死.

Original haiku (5-7-5 in on, each with exactly one autumn kigo, no 季重なり): 掬ひたる月こぼれけり子の手より (すくいたる/つきこぼれけり/このてより; 月) · 形見着て祖母のかたちに月を見る (かたみきて/そぼのかたちに/つきをみる; 月 — replaces 羽織着て…, because 羽織 is a winter word, 冬羽織) · 影ひとつ格子をのぼる良夜かな (かげひとつ/こうしをのぼる/りょうやかな; 良夜). Spare: ひとつ減る団子の山や今日の月 (今日の月). 障子 (winter) deliberately avoided. Credited as 創作 (原創 is Chinese usage).

Customs: fifteen 月見団子 stacked 9-4-2 (a common Kantō arrangement; regional variants exist); 衣かつぎ for 芋名月; お月見泥棒 is a regional children's custom; the fox-window chant varies too much by region and is never shown.

Costume: a six-year-old in everyday 紺絣 at a Shōwa home tsukimi wears a soft 兵児帯 (usually red or pink 絞り), not an 帯揚げ (which goes with a tied adult obi or a formal 七五三 outfit); a 78-year-old's obijime is subdued (海老茶/臙脂), not bright 朱.

Myth fidelity: 竹取物語 has no taboo against looking back (that is Izanagi's and Orpheus's); the text says the robe changes the wearer's heart — 「衣着せつる人は、心異になるなり」, 「物思ひなくなりにければ」 — so her look-back is framed as a heart not yet changed, not a broken rule. The old man does not split the bamboo with an axe: 「筒の中光りたり。それを見れば、三寸ばかりなる人、いとうつくしうてゐたり」 — the shadow-play has no axe.
Bells: in the Edo time-bell system 明け六つ was struck as six strokes after three preliminary 捨て鐘; the film's three strokes (215, 220, 225) are those 捨て鐘 — the hour itself is never heard.

Pigments: the unprint order is approximate — plant dyes first (紅 safflower and its 萩/鴇 pinks, plant yellows), then the blues, then mineral earths; 朱 vermilion is a stable mineral (丹 red lead darkens rather than fades); carbon never fades. Many ukiyo-e moons (Hiroshige's included) are left as bare paper, though some carry a tint, bokashi edge, mica or 胡粉 — the film's moon follows the bare-paper practice.
